The related project company, JFK NTO LLC, is developing, financing, constructing and will operate a roughly $9.5 billion, 2.6 million-square-foot international terminal with 23 gates under a long-term Port Authority lease. Carlyle originally held a 51% indirect project interest; at financial close on June 10, 2022, Ferrovial acquired 96% of that position and Carlyle retained approximately 2% indirect ownership. CAG remains the manager-level PortCo; JFK NTO LLC and the terminal are the associated project rather than separate PortCos. No later Carlyle full exit or signed divestiture was found through August 19, 2026. CAG's platform-level stake, precise legal entry date and current headquarters are not publicly disclosed.

owners.attributionRationale: The 2025 NYTDC New Terminal One official statement's sponsor table expressly identifies Carlyle Global Infrastructure Opportunity Fund (CGI) and states that CGI established CAG Holdings as its airport investment vehicle. Separately, the statement identifies CGI Phoenix Aggregator, L.P. as a Carlyle affiliate holding 4% of Mars, which owns 51% of project Topco. The fund attribution to CAG is disclosed; the exact intermediate Phoenix-to-fund chain and CAG platform-level percentage are not established by these disclosures. Preserve the existing qualified approximately 2% indirect project interest, also corroborated by Ferrovial's 2026 filed factbook; do not equate Mars-level percentages with platform equity.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

CAG Holdings is Carlyle's U.S. airport infrastructure platform associated with The New Terminal One at John F.

Kennedy International Airport. The related project company, JFK NTO LLC, is developing, financing, constructing and will operate a roughly $9.5 billion, 2.6 million-square-foot international terminal with 23 gates under a long-term Port Authority lease. Carlyle originally held a 51% indirect project interest; at financial close on June 10, 2022, Ferrovial acquired 96% of that position and Carlyle retained approximately 2% indirect ownership. Ferrovial's 2026 SEC materials report the current project split as Ferrovial 49%, Carlyle 2%, JLC Infrastructure 30% and Ullico Infrastructure 19%. CAG remains the manager-level PortCo; JFK NTO LLC and the terminal are the associated project rather than separate PortCos. No later Carlyle full exit or signed divestiture was found through August 19, 2026. CAG's platform-level stake, precise legal entry date and current headquarters are not publicly disclosed.

api.description: Braya Renewable Fuels is the manager-level renewable-fuels platform operating the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador through Braya Renewable Fuels (Newfoundland) LP. Cresta Fund Management acquired control in November 2021, while Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest. ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in April 2023. Exact sponsor percentages, voting rights and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed, and ECP Fund V is not directly supported for this investment. Commercial renewable-diesel operations began in February 2024; after a temporary 2025 shutdown, operations resumed, and the platform announced its first 100,000-barrel Canadian renewable-diesel sale in June 2026. Braya serves fuel markets in Canada, the United States, Mexico and Europe, while sustainable aviation fuel and green hydrogen or ammonia remain planned rather than confirmed commercial products. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Braya Renewable Fuels is the manager-level renewable-fuels platform operating the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador through Braya Renewable Fuels (Newfoundland) LP.

Cresta Fund Management acquired control in November 2021, while Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest. ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in April 2023. Exact sponsor percentages, voting rights and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed, and ECP Fund V is not directly supported for this investment. Commercial renewable-diesel operations began in February 2024; after a temporary 2025 shutdown, operations resumed, and the platform announced its first 100,000-barrel Canadian renewable-diesel sale in June 2026. Braya serves fuel markets in Canada, the United States, Mexico and Europe, while sustainable aviation fuel and green hydrogen or ammonia remain planned rather than confirmed commercial products. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

STORY TIMELINE
Feb 22, 2024
Expansion

Braya announced the start of commercial renewable-diesel operations at the Come By Chance refinery.

Apr 20, 2023
Investment

ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in Braya; the exact investing vehicle, percentage and voting rights were not publicly disclosed.

Nov 30, 2021
Investment

Cresta Fund Management closed its controlling investment in the Come By Chance refinery platform, which was rebranded Braya Renewable Fuels; Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest.
